title: PowerPoint on the web: attach and reference an image when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: Hold: the briefing leaves web applicability of connected-experience privacy controls open, although Microsoft documents that web experiences are controlled through Cloud Policy. The roadmap facts, licence-assignment path and PowerShell call are supported; the browser-policy checklist also has a minor table inconsistency.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The release note says this update does not alter security or privacy controls.
claims.quote: This update improves content integration without altering security or privacy controls.

claims.claim: The feature's release note describes no new permission, identity or sign-in step.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint reference attached images permissions sign-in admin; read the complete feature release-note entry and Copilot requirements. The entry documents prompt, attachment and review, with no new identity or permission step.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence gives access to the full Copilot experience in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users can use Copilot in PowerPoint without the add-on licence.

claims.claim: Chat experiences in Word, Excel and PowerPoint vary with licence and tenant configuration.

claims.claim: The included model describes a new option within the existing licensed Copilot in PowerPoint experience.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions: licensing
claims.claim: The specific Basic-versus-add-on entitlement for attached-image referencing is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot image licens Basic; PowerPoint Copilot Agent Mode reference image pricing. Read Copilot overview, requirements and feature release notes; general presentation/image editing is listed, but no attached-image-reference tier is specified.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No price specific to image referencing is published.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot Agent Mode reference image pricing; PowerPoint Copilot image licens Basic. Read Copilot overview, requirements and attached-image release notes; no feature-specific price appeared.

claims.claim: The roadmap and release note name no separate meter for image referencing.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot Agent Mode reference image pricing. Read the roadmap record, Copilot overview and attached-image release-note entry; none names an image-reference meter.

claims.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint for the web requires third-party cookies to be enabled.
claims.quote: For Copilot to work in Word for the web, Excel for the web, and PowerPoint for the web, third-party cookies must be enabled.

claims.claim: The roadmap record and feature release note state no administrator role for using image referencing.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint reference attached images permissions sign-in admin. Read the roadmap record and complete attached-image release-note entry; neither requires an administrator role to use it.

claims.claim: Licence assignment is reached in Microsoft 365 admin center through Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote:
In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page.
Select a product.
On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: The printed Set-MgUserLicense call assigns a licence to the specified user.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The documented licence-assignment control does not separately switch image attachment on or off.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot attach image admin disable. Read licence-assignment UI and PowerShell pages and configure-copilot-admin-center; they document licence/service assignment and other Copilot controls, not a separate attached-image-reference switch.

claims.claim: Turning off connected experiences that analyze content on devices disables Copilot features in PowerPoint and the other listed apps.
claims.quote:
If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps:
Excel
OneNote
Outlook
PowerPoint
Word

claims.claim: The privacy page names Windows, Mac, iOS and Android devices for the analyze-content control.
claims.quote: This applies to when you're running the most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.
claims.fix: Replace 'and it names Windows, Mac, iOS and Android devices' with 'and says this applies when running the most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS or Android devices'.

claims.claim: The cited privacy page does not name the web in its analyze-content applicability sentence.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint web connected experiences Cloud Policy. Read the cited privacy page's analyze-content section: its applicability sentence lists Windows, Mac, iOS and Android, not web.

claims.claim: Whether analyze-content connected-experience controls also apply to Copilot in PowerPoint for the web remains undocumented.
claims.quote:
Microsoft Copilot requires the Analyze Content connected experience category in Office to be enabled for Copilot to work in Microsoft 365 Apps, including Microsoft Teams.
The web experiences and modern apps are controlled exclusively by the Cloud Policy.
claims.fix: Replace the final Open questions bullet with: 'Microsoft's sensitive and regulated customer guidance says Copilot requires the Analyze Content connected experience category and that web experiences are controlled exclusively by Cloud Policy.' Cite and add to sources https://learn.microsoft.com/compliance/anz/blueprint-copilot-reqconfig#connected-experiences. Retain the narrower, accurate observation about the cited privacy sentence.

claims.where: summary; Governance controls; Open questions: administrator control
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no feature-specific administrator setting for attached-image referencing in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot attach image admin disable; Copilot PowerPoint attach reference image administrator disable policy. Read feature release notes and configure-copilot-admin-center; image generation and Vision controls are not an attachment-reference switch.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The feature is user-opt-in: users choose to attach an image, with no documented feature-specific admin enablement.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot attach image admin disable. Read release notes: 'Use the Copilot pane to enter a prompt and attach an image you want to use in your presentation.' Read Copilot admin settings; no image-reference enablement switch was documented.

claims.claim: No source describes a change to existing behaviour for users who do not attach an image.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint image referencing existing Agent Mode. Read the roadmap and complete attached-image release-note entry; both describe referencing an attached image, not changed behaviour for users who do not attach one.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions: Agent Mode
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described Agent Mode's handling of the attached image beyond the documented creation and review workflow.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint image referencing existing Agent Mode; PowerPoint Copilot Agent Mode reference image pricing. Read roadmap and attached-image release notes; no further image-specific Agent Mode mechanism was documented in relevant results.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The browser-policy check in the checklist has no corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote:
Check that browser policy allows third-party cookies for PowerPoint for the web.
The sole controls row governs which users hold the Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.fix: Replace the Before rollout browser-policy bullet with 'Confirm that Copilot works in PowerPoint for the web before communicating the feature.' Retain the documented third-party-cookie prerequisite in Scope; do not add a control row.
